transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 16:47 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Sam Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ben Cho (Redwood PSM); Jordan Lee (Acme SRE), Marta Alvarez (Acme Platform), Ravi Patel (Acme Product), Liam O'Connor (Acme Security)

Summary: quick sync on intermittent 5xxs and long tail queueing observed during peak 10-11am window. Agreed to gather targeted logs, run controlled benchmarks, and adjust adaptive-retry/backoff as well as transient routing to dedicated pool for spikes.

Topics: incident timeline, scope of affected requests, VPC egress/NAT considerations, retry/backoff policy, concurrency shaping, fallback to smaller model variant, security and compliance checklist request.

Action items (recap): see action_items metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sam Reyes: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, i see we have most people, quick agenda is incident follow up, replication steps, and next actions for the pilot.
[00:16] Jordan Lee: yeah, thanks Sam. we had a weird window thursday morning where a subset of requests hit long queue delays then intermittent 5xx from the inference layer, roughly 10:05 to 10:20 pacific. latency spikes around 8-12s for some calls.
[00:30] Marta Alvarez: to add, our app logs show client-side retries stacking up which made the situation worse. we had about ~180 concurrent user threads hitting the endpoint at that time, normally 60-70.
[00:44] Priya Nair: okay, can you confirm if those were bursts to the hosted endpoint or routed to your dedicated pool? sometimes routing policy will fallback to the cheaper variant and the KV cache warms slowly.
[00:58] Jordan Lee: they were hitting dedicated (we pinned) but i think some requests spilled to hosted when our dedicated pool hit its soft limit. the spillover looked like it used a slightly different model variant- not sure if that contributed.
[01:15] Ravi Patel: are we sure the 5xx were from the model server and not from a proxy/NAT timeout? our infra team flagged 504s at the load balancer.
[01:27] Ben Cho: i saw both 502 and 504 traces in the app logs we sampled. the Redwood runtime returns a 5xx when the model process OOMs or internal kernel fails, but network 504s are from upstream gateway timeouts; they look similar in dashboards.
[01:43] Jordan Lee: our initial correlate shows egress NAT saturation and retransmits; we pushed extra NAT capacity after. also some client retries had no jitter so they synchronized and amplified load.
[02:00] Priya Nair: makes sense. couple ideas we talked about: one, enforce client-side exponential backoff + jitter; two, adjust server-side adaptive retry to prefer short linear backoff on warm-cached tokens; three, divert overflow traffic to a smaller fast model variant as a graceful degradation.
[02:22] Liam O'Connor: from security perspective, we need to see audit logs and the VPC peering diagram before we approve any change to routing policies; also confirm that any fallback to hosted does not keep PII unredacted per our contract.
[02:38] Sam Reyes: noted, we'll add the networking diagram and SOC2 artifact. for PII we can configure redaction in the pipeline and set a policy to never send logs with user PII to hosted.
[02:52] Marta Alvarez: we also are concerned about tokenization differences across model variants causing output drift. if we fallback to a different model, the outputs must be consistent enough for downstream parsers.
[03:08] Priya Nair: agreed. when we tested last week, few prompts showed small differences but we can run a focused eval on your critical prompt set to measure drift. i'll include exact metrics (EM, BLEU-ish heuristics, and pass-rate for rules).
[03:26] Jordan Lee: on the replication side, what's the minimal dataset you need from us? we can send a 200-request sample if that's enough.
[03:33] Priya Nair: yes a 200-300 sample that covers the long-tail prompts and includes request IDs is perfect; include corresponding timestamps and response sizes. ideally include any request headers that may affect routing (customer-id, region).
[03:47] Ben Cho: one more note, our telemetry shows increased KV cache misses during the spike window which increases per-request work. that suggests the spillover requests didn't have warmed KV cache and caused cpu/kernel pressure.
[04:02] Jordan Lee: can you explain that KV cash bit - sorry sometimes i mishear your terminology.
[04:08] Priya Nair: sure - K V cache, it's the key value cache for the transformer past-key-values. when the cache isn't warmed, every request does full autoregressive compute and costs more cycles; warming requires repeated or prefix-similar queries.
[04:24] Marta Alvarez: okay so the mitigation is either keep sticky routing so warmed workers get sticky traffic or accept higher cost while we warm the cache?
[04:33] Priya Nair: yes, sticky routing or priority busting to keep hot workers pinned. Redwood can also do prefix caching on our edge to reduce cold-start phi but sticky routing is simplest.
[04:47] Jordan Lee: about retries, our code does immediate retries up to 3 times with no backoff. should we change to exponential backoff with jitter?
[04:57] Sam Reyes: strongly recommend exponential backoff with randomized jitter; immediate retries are the classic thundering herd. cloud native patterns are 100-500ms initial with exponential. we'll share sample libs.
[05:12] Ravi Patel: what about rate-limiting at edge - can Redwood enforce per-customer token-rate or concurrent request caps?
[05:20] Priya Nair: yes, we have per-API-key concurrency caps and token-rate quotas. for pilots we often suggest a soft concurrency limit plus a burst window. we can route excess to a lower-cost queue or emit 429s depending on your preference.
[05:36] Liam O'Connor: if we emit 429s, we need clear client handling and metrics. also for SOC2 we need evidence of rate limit rules and audit proof.
[05:47] Sam Reyes: we'll include the rate limit config and audit logs export sample.
[05:53] Jordan Lee: on the logs, what exact request IDs do you need? we've got the full trace but it's noisy.
[06:00] Priya Nair: capture three request IDs from the 10:05-10:20 window that experienced 5xxs and include worker hostnames and timestamps; also the raw model-server logs around those timestamps.
[06:13] Jordan Lee: ok we'll extract and share via the secure link.
[06:18] Marta Alvarez: is there a recommended retry matrix we should adopt short-term? we just want something pragmatic to avoid cascading failures.
[06:26] Priya Nair: short-term: client retries = 2 max, base 250ms with jitter, exponential factor 2; server-side adaptive: initial 50ms linear backoff for known warm-cache hits, escalate to exponential for cold starts, and drop to fallback queue after N attempts. we'll document exact numbers in the follow-up.
[06:46] Ben Cho: additionally, consider a circuit-breaker threshold on the dedicated pool that flips traffic to fallback after sustained error rate > 5% for 2 minutes. that prevents long tail impact.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: sounds good. question on fallback model variant — is there an automatic quantized variant that preserves functionality but reduces latency?
[07:07] Priya Nair: yes, we have quantized 4-bit variants that shave latency and have lower memory. Redwood Optimize can recommend which variant based on your prompt length distribution; i'll run a quick suggestion.
[07:20] Ravi Patel: how do we measure output quality drift when switching variants? we need deterministic checks to gate fallback.
[07:29] Priya Nair: use a validation prompt set and define pass/fail thresholds (e.g. 95% pass-rate on critical assertions). Redwood's eval harness can run this during pilot and produce a regression alert.
[07:41] Liam O'Connor: also need confirmation on data retention and logs—if any data goes to hosted fallback, is it retained under Redwood's default retention or can we request custom retention and deletion?
[07:54] Sam Reyes: hosted fallback uses default retention but for enterprise accounts we support retention policies and can set auto-deletion hooks; we'll include the policy and options in the security pack.
[08:08] Jordan Lee: ok, plan seems clear. two further asks: can Redwood simulate a soak test for 20 minutes at 2x peak so we can see behavior, and can you run a runbook playbook with our SREs to practice failover?
[08:22] Priya Nair: yes to both; we'll schedule a soak test in staging and run a joint tabletop with your SREs. propose next wed 05/13 for the tabletop unless you prefer earlier.
[08:34] Jordan Lee: 05/13 works.
[08:37] Sam Reyes: great. circling back: i'll send the security docs + network diagram; Priya will run the adaptive retry matrix and a small quantized-model eval; Jordan will pull the request ids and NAT logs. we reconvene next week.
[08:55] Marta Alvarez: one more micro item — can Redwood add a header that indicates model-variant in the response so we can see what was used? helps debugging.
[09:02] Priya Nair: yes we can add an optional response header x-redwood-model-variant, configurable per deployment. we'll include that in the follow-up.
[09:12] Ravi Patel: nice, that'll help correlate output differences.
[09:18] Sam Reyes: ok we'll wrap. thanks everyone. summary and action items in the follow-up email.
[09:25] Meeting end: 17:33 PDT
